title: Can LLMs Introspect? A Reality Check
abstract: arXiv:2605.26242v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Can large language models detect and report their own internal states? A number of recent studies have argued that they can. Drawing on lessons from human metacognition research, we argue that this conclusion may be premature. We identify two conditions that a paradigm needs to meet in order to establish introspection. First, the test needs to require privileged access: it should not be solvable using cues available in the input. Second, it needs to require second-order computation: second-order, meta-representations of first-order, task-related representations. This condition cannot be satisfied by task performance alone: it requires designs under which second-order and first-order accounts make divergent predictions. We re-examine two paradigms that have been used to argue for model introspection in light of these conditions. translated_title: 大语言模型能否内省？现实检验
translated_abstract: 大语言模型能否检测并报告它们自身的内部状态？最近的一些研究认为它们可以。借鉴人类元认知研究的经验，我们认为这一结论可能为时过早。我们确定了两个条件，一个范式需要满足这些条件才能确立内省能力。首先，测试需要要求特权访问：它不应能通过输入中可用的线索来解决。其次，它需要二阶计算：对一阶、任务相关表征的二阶元表征。这一条件无法仅通过任务性能来满足：它需要设计使二阶和一阶解释产生不同预测。我们根据这些条件重新审视了两种曾被用来论证模型内省的范式。在第一种范式中，模型必须预测源自其自身隐藏状态的标签；我们发现分类器能……
tldr: 本文指出，现有证明大语言模型具有内省能力的研究可能过于草率，因为其测试范式未满足特权访问和二阶计算两个关键条件，导致结论缺乏充分依据。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that existing evidence for LLM introspection is premature, as the test paradigms fail to meet two critical conditions—privileged access and second-order computation—making the conclusions insufficiently supported.
